text: If thy neighbour dislike thee, change the gate of thy house.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Suit thy business to thy circumstances.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Ask assistance from those only who have the power of helping thee.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Every one knows best his own affairs, and those interested in them.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: The one-eyed person is a beauty in the country of the blind.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: To have patience with a friend rather than lose him for ever.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: The fool has his answer on the edge of his tongue.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Rather take from the fool, than give to the wise.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Cut up the evil by the root.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Expel avidity from thy heart; the fetters will be loosened from thy foot.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: The talents of a person are less admired at home than abroad.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: The rejoicing of the envious rends the heart.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: A thing that does not satiate, creates hunger.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: The guest of the hospitable treats hospitably.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: The enmity of the wise, rather than the friendship of the fool.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: The embrace at meeting is better than that at parting.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: The eye of the sun cannot be hidden.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: The dog does not bark in his own house.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Riches have disclosed in thy character the bad qualities formerly concealed by thy poverty.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Who gives not thanks to men, gives not thanks to God.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Who knocks at the door will hear the answer.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Every thing crooked-necked is not a camel.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: He who is not ashamed does whatever he likes.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Advice given in the midst of a crowd is loathsome.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Times are so bad that even Pharaoh is regretted.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: On the day of victory no fatigue is felt.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Thy right hand knows nothing of thy left hand.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: The eye-witness observes what the absent does not see.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)

text: Do not beat the wolf, and do not cause hunger to the sheep.
source: Arabic Proverbs (collected at Cairo by Burckhardt)
